description: Public-facing site for a city's Civic Dining Program — a chronological archive of community meals, neighborhood pop-ups, and food-policy milestones run by the municipal Food & Culture Office, aimed at residents who track local food culture closely

pages.name: timeline
pages.description: Chronological archive of every civic meal and food-policy event, year by year
components: Top bar with the program seal, the office name 'Department of Food & Culture', a primary nav (Timeline, Menus, Venues, Policy, About), and a small 'EN / ES / 中文' language switcher
Page header with title 'A Public Record of Civic Meals', a one-sentence mission line, and a filter strip with a year-range slider, category multi-select, and neighborhood dropdown

Vertical timeline running down the center — alternating left/right entry cards anchored to a spine of date dots, each card showing date, event name, neighborhood tag, category chip, two-line summary, attendance count, and a 'View menu' link
Decade jump-rail pinned to the side — vertical list of decade labels (2010s, 2020s) with sub-items per year, highlighting the year currently in view
Footer with office address, public-records request link, accessibility statement, open-data CSV download of the full timeline, and the city seal

pages.name: menus
pages.description: Browsable index of every menu served at civic events, treated like a permanent municipal record
components: Same top bar
Page heading 'Menu Archive' with a count of total menus on file and a sort dropdown (Most recent, Oldest, By chef, By neighborhood)

Filter rail on the left with checkboxes for course type (Starter, Main, Side, Dessert, Beverage), dietary tags (Vegan, Halal, Kosher, Gluten-free), sourcing radius slider in miles, and a season chip row (Spring, Summer, Fall, Winter)

Grid of menu cards (three per row) — each card shows event date, event name, presiding chef, an indexed course list with prices marked 'Free / Civic', a sourcing-radius badge, and a 'Read full menu' link

pages.name: menu-detail
pages.description: Single archived menu rendered as an official document with provenance
components: Same top bar
Document header with event title, date, venue, presiding chef, attendance, and a row of metadata pills (record number, filed-by clerk, archived-on date)
Two-column menu body — left column lists numbered courses with dish name, description, and dietary icons; right column is a 'Sourcing ledger' table mapping each ingredient to its supplier
Footnotes section below the menu with a chef's note paragraph, a translator credit, and an allergen disclosure block
Provenance footer bar with previous-menu and next-menu navigation arrows, a 'Cite this record' button that reveals a citation string, and a 'Download as PDF' link

pages.name: venues
pages.description: Directory of public venues that have hosted civic meals
components: Same top bar
Page heading 'Civic Venues' with a toggle between Map view and List view and a search input for venue name or address

Map-plus-list split — left half is an interactive map with numbered pins clustered by district, right half is a scrollable list of venue rows (each row: pin number, venue name, address, district, total events hosted, first-hosted date, capacity)

Selected-venue side panel that slides in with the venue photo block, an accessibility checklist (ramp, elevator, hearing loop, gender-neutral restrooms), a list of upcoming bookings, and a 'Request this venue' civic-form button

pages.name: policy
pages.description: Public log of food-policy decisions tied to the dining program
components: Same top bar
Page heading 'Policy & Ordinances' with a short paragraph explaining how the dining program intersects with municipal code

Chronological ordinance list — each entry has ordinance number, enactment date, title, sponsoring council member, a two-sentence summary, a status chip (In effect, Amended, Repealed), and links to the full text and the vote record
Sidebar with a 'Currently in deliberation' list of three pending items, each showing committee name, next hearing date, and a 'Submit public comment' link
Bottom panel 'How a meal becomes policy' — a horizontal five-step process diagram with numbered stages (Proposal, Community input, Committee review, Council vote, Implementation)

pages.name: about
pages.description: About page describing the Civic Dining Program, its staff, and how to participate
components: Same top bar
Mandate block with the program's founding statement, founding date, and the name of the council resolution that established it
Staff roster grid (three per row) — each entry has a portrait placeholder, name, civic title, office phone extension, and public email
Get-involved section with three side-by-side cards: 'Propose a meal' (form link), 'Volunteer as a server' (calendar link), 'Nominate a venue' (form link)
Footer (same as timeline page)
